gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-gunjal: Stencilia stands structural and striking, its curves left gapped at the ends. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi does the quieter work, with tall, crayon-thick lowercase strokes that carry the text while the heading takes the attention.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-gurmuk: Blocky, bold-faced and a bit rebellious, Stencilia breaks its curves open at the terminals. Noto Sans Gurmukhi follows with outward-pointing, tong-like ends and low ascenders, so the heading is best given generous size.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-hanuno: Stencilia's most distinctive habit is the spacious gap it leaves where each curve ends, which gives it a cut-out, structural look. And Noto Sans Hanunoo makes that boldness easy to live with, since its lowercase fills most of the height and its terminals stay open.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Stencilia is structural and striking, with gaps cut into its curves. Noto Sans Hebrew would read smoothly over many lines, its dominant midsection and wide curve openings keeping the text feeling spacious and modern.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-hk: Striking is the first word for Stencilia, whose curves stop short and leave visible gaps at their ends. And Noto Sans HK gives it a counterweight, with large lowercase forms and lifted brush ends that make the pair's difference in character its best asset.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-imperi: Cut-out, sturdy and a little theatrical, Stencilia leaves gaps where its curves end. But Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic would feel lost if the heading were shrunk small, since its pincer-like c and short capital step are the gentler, friendlier voice here.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-inscri: Stencil-cut and structural, Stencilia looks like it was punched out of sheet metal. And it earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian brings big open eyes on its e and a and a deep middle band.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-jp: Stencilia is the striking one, its curve ends left open and its ascenders sitting compactly above the x-height. Noto Sans JP is built for steady text, with a very tall x-height and sweeping curves.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-kannad: Approachable is the mood Noto Sans Kannada sets, with its gentle step up to capitals and s curves that open wide at both ends. And a longer stretch of it would read easily beneath Stencilia, whose gapped curves supply all the structure.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-kayah-: Stencilia's curve terminals are spaced wide apart, giving it a cut, structural look. It does its best work as a bold statement, whereas Noto Sans Kayah Li stays understated, with lifted brush ends and capitals only slightly above the lowercase.
